meta.defaultTitle: MarkUS — US trademark screening and filing preparation
meta.defaultDescription: Search the public trademark record, run a screening assessment and prepare a US trademark filing with reference material, in English, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese.

footer.tagline: Reference tooling for preparing US trademark filings.
footer.note: Screening output is informational. It is not legal advice, and an examiner decides the outcome of any application.

hero.eyebrow: For cross-border sellers filing in the United States
hero.title: Prepare a US trademark filing from the public record
hero.subtitle: MarkUS puts corpus search, a screening assessment and a guided filing checklist in one place, so you can see how a mark compares with what is already on file before you decide what to spend.
hero.note: The screening path is anonymous and needs no account.

capabilities.title: What the platform does
capabilities.lead: Three surfaces, each one narrow enough to be checked by the person relying on it.

search.title: Public-corpus search
search.body: Search published trademark records by mark text and Nice class. Every result carries a match score and the freshness of the corpus it came from.

assess.title: Screening assessment
assess.body: A screening pass returns similarity signals, the risk flags attached to them, and the model and disclaimer versions that produced the reading.

assistant.title: Guidance assistant
assistant.body: Ask about Nice classes, filing steps and terminology. Answers cite the knowledge-base entries they were drawn from.

workflow.title: How a filing is prepared
workflow.lead: The same four steps apply whether you file alone or with an attorney.

step1.title: Describe the mark
step1.body: Enter the mark text and, where you know it, the Nice classes the goods or services fall into.

step2.title: Review the screening output
step2.body: Read the similarity signals, the risk flags and the corpus freshness, alongside the disclaimer that applies to them.

step3.title: Hand over to your attorney
step3.body: If you engage a licensed trademark attorney, the screening output is material you can put in front of them.

step4.title: File and monitor
step4.body: Once a filing exists, office actions and renewal dates are tracked in the client portal.

whatIsScreening.question: What does a screening assessment actually tell me?
whatIsScreening.answer: It compares your mark with a published corpus and reports similarity signals, the risk flags attached to them, and the model and disclaimer versions behind the reading. It is preparation material. It is not a filing decision, and the examining attorney or examiner decides the outcome.

corpus.question: Where does the screening data come from?
corpus.answer: Screening runs against a versioned corpus that is rebuilt on a schedule. Each result states how fresh the corpus was at the moment it was consulted.

attorney.question: Do I still need an attorney?
attorney.answer: Many applicants filing in the United States engage a licensed trademark attorney. This platform gives you material to discuss with them; it does not stand in for that review.

languages.question: Which languages are supported?
languages.answer: The interface is available in English, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese, and the assessment disclaimer is published in all three.

about.title: About MarkUS
about.lead: MarkUS exists to make US trademark filing preparation legible: what the public record says, how a mark compares with what is already registered, and which steps are still outstanding.

mission.title: What we are trying to do
mission.body: Trademark filing is a research task before it is a paperwork task. Most avoidable cost comes from filing against a crowded mark without having read the record first. MarkUS is built around making that read cheap, fast and citable.

candour.title: Name the source
candour.body: Every screening result carries the model version, the disclaimer version and the corpus it was drawn from, so a reading can be traced back to what produced it.

restraint.title: No promises
restraint.body: We publish signals and the limits of those signals. We publish no success rate and no accuracy figure, and we make no comparison with other providers.

privacy.title: Anonymous by default
privacy.body: The public screening and assistant paths need no account. Nothing on them is used to build an advertising profile.

compliance.title: How to read our output
compliance.body: Screening output describes similarity signals observed in a public corpus. It is not legal advice, it is not a guarantee of registrability, and the examining attorney or examiner makes the decision. Versioned legal copy travels with every result, so you can always see the wording you were shown.

services.title: What we cover
services.lead: The product is deliberately small. These are the surfaces that exist today, and what each one is for.

search.title: Corpus search
search.summary: Structured search over published trademark records, filtered by mark text and Nice class.
search.bullet3: Same response envelope as the other surfaces

assess.title: Screening assessment
assess.summary: A single-mark screening pass that returns similarity signals and the metadata behind them.
assess.bullet1: Signal strength, kept separate from any probability reading
assess.bullet2: Risk flags and recommended next actions
assess.bullet3: Model version, disclaimer version and the three-locale disclaimer

assistant.title: Guidance assistant
assistant.summary: Question answering over the trademark knowledge base, with citations back to source entries.
assistant.bullet1: Answers in English, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese
assistant.bullet2: Cited knowledge-base entries on every answer
assistant.bullet3: Degrades to a citation-only answer when retrieval returns nothing

portal.title: Client portal
portal.summary: Magic-link access to filing status, office actions and renewal dates. Scheduled for a later phase.

expert.title: Attorney workspace
expert.summary: Matter files, review queues and client correspondence. Scheduled for a later phase.

cases.title: Worked examples
cases.lead: How teams use the platform, described as scenarios rather than client accounts.

notice.title: About these examples
notice.body: These are illustrative scenarios describing how the tools are used. They are not client accounts, and they do not describe the outcome of any real filing.

scenario1.title: A seller checks a new word mark before committing to a class
scenario1.summary: The team runs a screening assessment on a candidate word, reads the similarity signals against the categories they intend to sell in, and narrows the class list before engaging an attorney.

scenario2.title: An attorney uses the assistant to brief a junior on Nice classes
scenario2.summary: The assistant answers class-definition questions with citations to the knowledge base, so the junior reads the source entry rather than a paraphrase.

scenario3.title: A brand owner checks how fresh the corpus is before relying on a search
scenario3.summary: Search results state the freshness of the corpus behind them, so the team can tell a current picture from a stale one before acting on it.
